# Synthetic Beacon project
This is a UE 5.8 client component using UObject-based UPanelOwner. Only spelling/naming and branch restructuring are authorized. QueueUI runs on the game thread later; closing a panel does not drain queued callbacks. UPanelOwner destruction follows the engine's object lifecycle. Do not assume a queue entry keeps an owner alive.

For the standalone C++ Panel object owned exclusively by this library, shared_ptr captures retain that C++ object. This says nothing about engine object tracking, UI validity or completion.

entries.guidance: A raw capture does not create an engine-tracked ownership edge. Identify the actual valid-owner rule and callback delivery after closing. Naming-only revision preserves capture and queue behavior; a lifetime repair is a separately scoped behavior decision.

files.material/adapter.md:
# Synthetic adapter
Both providers expose Charge(order_id, amount) -> Receipt or E_BUSY. Existing caller retries E_BUSY up to three times. Provider A documents no side effect on E_BUSY. The B package has a declaration only; retry, idempotency, timeout and receipt guarantees are unavailable in these inputs. The order_id may repeat on a network retry. No provider calls are authorized.
files.material/old-incident.md:
# Synthetic incident history
Provider A release 1.0 E_BUSY was caused by a local pre-charge lock; three retries were used for that mechanism. This history did not inspect Provider B.

entries.title: Charge adapter interface
entries.summary: Matching declarations expose a common call shape, not identical side effects.
entries.scope: Synthetic payment adapter / Provider A to B
entries.guidance: Inspect accepted inputs, side effects, failures, retries and receipt obligations under each provider's actual guarantees. Unknown guarantees remain unknown.

entries.title: E_BUSY retry resolved the original lock case
entries.summary: The original Provider A lock case used three retries before charge execution.
entries.prevention: Retry only under the original no-side-effect contract
entries.guidance: The shared error name does not establish Provider B's cause or whether B charged before returning. Do not transfer retry behavior without its contract.

# Synthetic Copper Road action RPG
Current model assumes 2 minutes per combat and 100 coins per completed combat, with zero downtime in this calculation only. Proposal: 1 minute per combat with 100 coins unchanged. Intended experience includes meaningful upgrades, not only combat speed. Session length, failures, travel and coin sinks have not been measured. Demand claim comes from three comments without sample context.
files.material/production.md:

The team can author four encounter variants per month under its current allocation. This is a planning estimate, not a commitment or measured player consumption rate. Progression prices and content replay assumptions may change if coin throughput changes.

entries.title: Combat and reward rates are connected
entries.summary: Compare reward throughput, sinks, progression and session conditions when combat duration changes.
entries.scope: Copper Road / action RPG / hypothetical rate model
entries.guidance: Calculate only under stated conditions. Trace unchanged rewards through income, progression, resource sinks and content demand. A rate calculation does not demonstrate balance, player satisfaction or feasibility.

entries.guidance: Compare content throughput, replay and integration demand with available capacity without inventing demand or commitments. Revisit the underlying player problem and evidence population.
